title: Amplitude and Period of a sin(bx) and a cos(bx)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: State the amplitude and period of y = a sin(bx) and y = a cos(bx), and explain what each parameter changes on the graph.
finalAnswer: Both curves have amplitude $|a|$ and period $\dfrac{2\pi}{|b|}$; $a$ scales the height and $b$ compresses or stretches the wave horizontally.

steps.title: Identify the Amplitude
steps.explanation: Since sin and cos oscillate between -1 and 1, multiplying by a makes the wave swing between -|a| and |a|. The amplitude measures the height of one swing from the midline, so it is always nonnegative.
steps.why: Using |a| rather than a guards against the sign of a being mistaken for a size.

steps.title: Derive the Period
steps.explanation: The parent wave completes a cycle when its angle grows by 2*pi. For y = a sin(bx), the angle bx grows by 2*pi when x grows by 2*pi/|b|, so that quotient is the period. Larger |b| packs more cycles into the same interval.
steps.why: Tracking when the inner angle advances by 2*pi gives the period without memorization.

steps.title: Check with Concrete Values
steps.explanation: For y = 3 sin(2x), the graph peaks at 3 and repeats every pi units. For y = -cos(4x), the amplitude is |-1| = 1 and the period is 2*pi/4 = pi/2; the negative sign flips the wave but changes neither measure.
steps.why: Testing one sine and one reflected cosine confirms the formulas apply to both curves identically.
